raw:
The pole sitter won 13 of the 21 races in 2016.

I checked each race's top-10 result and grid positions. Where the winner started from grid 1, that race counts:

| Round | Race | Winner | Grid | Pole won? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Australia | Rosberg | 2 | No |
| 2 | Bahrain | Rosberg | 2 | No |
| 3 | China | Rosberg | 1 | Yes |
| 4 | Russia | Rosberg | 1 | Yes |
| 5 | Spain | Verstappen | 4 | No |
| 6 | Monaco | Hamilton | 3 | No |
| 7 | Canada | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |
| 8 | Europe (Baku) | Rosberg | 1 | Yes |
| 9 | Austria | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |
| 10 | Britain | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |
| 11 | Hungary | Hamilton | 2 | No |
| 12 | Germany | Hamilton | 2 | No |
| 13 | Belgium | Rosberg | 1 | Yes |
| 14 | Italy | Rosberg | 2 | No |
| 15 | Singapore | Rosberg | 1 | Yes |
| 16 | Malaysia | Ricciardo | 4 | No |
| 17 | Japan | Rosberg | 1 | Yes |
| 18 | United States | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |
| 19 | Mexico | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |
| 20 | Brazil | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |
| 21 | Abu Dhabi | Hamilton | 1 | Yes |

That gives 13 pole-to-win races: Rosberg 6 (China, Russia, Europe, Belgium, Singapore, Japan) and Hamilton 7 (Canada, Austria, Britain, United States, Mexico, Brazil, Abu Dhabi). The 8 others were won from a different grid slot.

The season standings are consistent with these results: Rosberg 9 wins, Hamilton 10 wins, Ricciardo 1, Verstappen 1, totalling 21.

ANSWER: 13
